result.title: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models
result.summary: Industries are increasingly adopting AI-driven systems to automate a wide range of tasks, including high-stakes decisions in human resources, such as candidate screening and recruitment. This makes evaluating their fairness essential, particularly when decisions directly affect individuals' opportunities. Accordingly, the EU AI Act classifies recruitment AI systems as high-risk, imposing strict requirements on their deployment. In this context, compact ``System~1'' decision models offer a fast and cost-efficient alternative to general-purpose LLMs, yet their fairness remains largely unexplored. This article presents the first systematic bias and fairness audit of \jev{}, a typed-decision model targeting recruitment applications. The study evaluates how explicit demographic attributes and implicit candidate cues influence screening scores, rankings, and shortlisting outcomes. These effects are compared against a noise floor derived from name substitutions and typographical variations. The evaluation also examines output validity, latency, and cost. Counterfactual CV datasets and evaluation code are released for reproducibility.

AI.brief_summary: 该文对面向招聘筛选的紧凑型「System 1」类型化决策模型做偏见与公平性审计，考察显式人口属性与隐式候选人线索对评分、排序和入围结果的影响，并与噪声基线比较，同时报告输出有效性、时延与成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究主题是招聘决策模型的公平性审计，虽提及推理时延与成本，但不涉及视觉或多模态表征、latent 推理状态、证据获取与停止决策，缺乏可核查的实质联系。
